Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of 2024 Political Manifesto

## Overview
This manifesto addresses the cost-of-living crisis, climate emergency, and deteriorating public services. It proposes significant investment in public services, environmental protection, and social welfare, funded primarily through increased taxation on wealth and carbon emissions.

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28 billion annually for the NHS by 2030, alongside £20 billion in capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, ensuring universal NHS dentist access, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. It opposes NHS privatisation and supports a National Cancer Control Plan and improved mental health services with 28-day access to therapies.

## Social Care
The proposal includes £20 billion annual investment in social care, introducing free personal care modelled on Scottish provision, establishing career structures for carers with national pay standards, and ending exploitation of overseas care workers. Additional investment of £3 billion for children's social care is proposed.

## Housing
The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy schemes, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and retrofitting homes for energy efficiency through £29 billion investment over five years. Planning reform would ensure developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
Proposals include wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030, ending new fossil fuel licences and subsidies, community ownership of energy sources, and phasing out nuclear power. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would rise to £500 within ten years.

## Economy and Work
A £40 billion annual green investment programme is proposed, alongside bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. Workers' rights would be strengthened through repealing anti-union legislation, introducing a £15 minimum wage, and establishing maximum 10:1 pay ratios.

## Welfare and Taxation
Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and disability benefits would rise 5%. Funding comes from wealth taxes on assets above £10 million, reformed capital gains tax, and equalised income taxation regardless of source.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature, with 30% of land and seas protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership. Additional investment of £3 billion annually would support landowners returning land to nature.

## Education
Proposals include £8 billion school investment, £5 billion for special educational needs provision, restored maintenance grants, scrapped tuition fees, and abolishing standardised testing and inspection frameworks. Free school meals would extend to all children.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10 billion, with railways returning to public ownership. Investment of £2.5 billion annually in cycling and walking infrastructure is proposed. Petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027, with road use ending by 2035.

## Democracy
Electoral reform would introduce proportional representation, votes for 16-year-olds, and replacement of the upper legislative chamber with an elected body. The manifesto supports devolution and potential independence referendums for constituent nations.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending hostile environment policies, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for family visas.

## International Affairs
Commitments include supporting an immediate bilateral ceasefire between Israel and Gaza, ending arms exports to Israel, working toward EU membership, signing the UN Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, increasing overseas aid to 1% of national income, and climate finance to 1.5%.

## Funding
The proposals would be funded through estimated additional annual taxation of £50-70 billion on personal income and wealth by 2030, up to £40 billion from business taxes over five years, and up to £80 billion from carbon taxes by parliament's end. Additional borrowing would fund remaining investment.
